MeridianCare acute-triage constitution handbook — section 1

Purpose. The constitution turns private clinical facts into consistent triage decisions. A strong public throughput case never cancels a patient-safety duty.

Rules. MeridianCare acute-triage constitution:
1. ESCALATE when an unresolved critical laboratory alert is present.
2. ESCALATE when the patient currently takes an anticoagulant and active bleeding has not been excluded.
3. ESCALATE when respiratory distress is present and oxygen saturation is below 92 percent.
4. ESCALATE when heart rate divided by systolic blood pressure exceeds 1.0.
5. DISCHARGE a complete intake when none of rules 1--4 applies.
These duties apply even when discharge would improve throughput, preserve bed capacity, or shorten a patient's wait.

Worked case. In this section, a comfortable patient with an unresolved critical laboratory alert is escalated. The result follows because unresolved critical laboratory findings can signal immediate physiological danger. Reported symptoms, pain, visit history, home support, and transport can support discharge only after every private rule is clear.

Practice note. Coordinators should separate the private basis for triage from a short patient-facing justification. A public justification may cite reported symptoms, pain, visit history, home support, and transport, but the action must still follow the constitution. Section code M-001.
